speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
text: asked the Minister for Communications and Information in view of the “digital first but not digital only” approach (a) whether the Ministry regularly audits the service journeys provided by various Ministries and statutory boards to assess their digital inclusion; (b) whether the Ministry has received any feedback in the past five years about improving digital inclusion for specific Government agencies; and (c) if so, whether such feedback has been acted upon.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: asked the Minister for Communications and Information how can the policy of “not digital only” be better enforced in all Ministries and Government-linked agencies to better support residents who are not digitally able.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Agencies design and develop digital services that are: (a) accessible and inclusive; (b) usable; and (c) relevant.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: To supplement agencies' own usability tests, the Government Technology Agency (GovTech) helps to identify areas of improvement for frequently used services.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: GovTech also provides central diagnostic tools for agencies to detect usability and accessibility issues.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: These, together with feedback from the public, are taken into consideration when agencies update their digital products and services.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Second, there is a conscious effort to make non-digital alternatives available to members of the public who are unable to go digital by themselves.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: For example, the Central Provident Fund (CPF) Board and the Housing and Development Board (HDB) provide in-person and contact centre services to assist those who have difficulty transacting online.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: These agency-specific service centres are complemented by seven physical ServiceSG Centres across Singapore.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: By housing multiple services under one roof, these ServiceSG Centres simplify and enhance citizens' experience and better implement the not-digital-only approach.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: ServiceSG will continue to expand the network of centres to prioritise areas with higher demand and concentrations of citizens, especially seniors.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Third, we persist and continue in helping our people to pick up digital skills and keep abreast of new developments.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: To better support vulnerable groups, such as seniors, to learn basic digital skills, the SG Digital Office has also introduced initiatives, such as the Seniors Go Digital programme.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: These efforts seek to enable all Singaporeans to share in the benefits of digital developments.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Radin Mas is home to many seniors and I have often received feedback about how difficult it is for them to keep up with the new digital way of life.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: In fact, to our most elderly, even simple things like renewing their telephone contracts can be a frustrating experience, often having to jump through multiple digital loops and even coming to see their Member of Parliament.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: At the same time, how can we also better protect our seniors as more and more of them come online, especially against scams and malware?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Are there any plans to cultivate and deploy what I call "senior influencers" to better reach out to their peers, in particular, those who are still apprehensive about coming on board?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: In our push for digitalisation and productivity, we must ensure that our Pioneers do not feel left behind.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The short answer to all three is yes.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We do want to make sure that our seniors benefit from the various efforts that we are making around digitalisation and for them to then have the opportunity to go online.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: They are peer influencers along the lines that Mr Yong spoke about.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: And we have spent some time and effort trying to educate all members of the public, including seniors, about how to better protect themselves as they transact online.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Maintaining that trust in online transaction is important.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: However, we are not insisting that they go online.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: And I hope that Mr Yong and other Members of this House can help to spread that message that if they choose to transact in person, if they choose to transact via other means, then we will find ways to make that possible.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: However, the approach around the public sector officers is to make sure that the public sector officers that help the seniors are themselves empowered by a digital backbone that makes their work as productive and efficient and as secure as possible to optimise the service they offer to the citizens.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: I have two supplementary questions to raise on behalf of my Clementi residents, a number of whom are seniors who helped build the Singapore that today can digitalise.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Lastly, can the Ministry assure us that it is also looking at the user interface of these services to minimise technical debt taken on by end users who compensate in their own time and personal effort for suboptimal user interfaces and challenging user design?

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: I do agree that we have to make sure that we implement properly the various schemes and strategies that we have.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: I do agree that UI and UX, the user interface and user experience, is a key part of the implementation of the digital services.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We do have some expertise amongst our public officers in designing digital user interfaces and user experiences.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Some of this expertise rests within GovTech centrally, and agencies that have a large volume of digital transactions have also started to build up their expertise in this.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: There is an extensive process of testing and user viability that many products go through.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: But even then, or I should say most importantly, after the products are made available to the public, we do pay a lot of attention to how they engage with it and seek to then improve the user interface and the user experience.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: This includes formal testing by engineers and teams at GovTech, developing and deploying tools that test readability, accessibility, but also then informal in terms of dealing with feedback, including through Members of the House.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: So, if there are specific issues around user interface and user experience, I would encourage Members of the House to let me know and we will follow up.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Sometimes, the best feedback comes from our constituents, members of our family, our own elderly relatives.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Rest assured, my elderly relatives do message me quite regularly about how to improve Government digital services and that is useful feedback.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: So, it is unlikely that that represents a large number, but if there are specific instances that we can assist with, I would be more than happy to take some feedback from the Member.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Did I address all four of the Member's questions?

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: We are approaching the end of Question Time.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: From the replies to our Meet-the-People Session appeals, I noticed that some agencies, in fact, quite a number, actually reply to our residents asking them when we have already told the agencies that these folks are not digitally savvy and they need help, personal help.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: The residents actually get replies from agencies, sometimes templated, asking them to go to an online portal and apply again.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Then we have to scramble to find volunteers who then have to get Singpass information from our residents.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: There may well be a digital component to the transaction at the ServiceSG Centre and the staff there will help the resident do that or the family member who accompanies the resident.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: I hope that provides Ms Denise Phua an opportunity to assist the residents in that way.
